what: Behind the board, a transparent WebGL canvas holds twenty-two thin-pressed triangular glass pieces (transmission 1 · refraction 1.45 · thickness .35 · coat 1) floating, each turning slowly (±.2rad per second). Each time the board scrolls one screen height the pieces flow upward at 1.2~2x speed so top and bottom wrap, the group tilts 8% toward the cursor, and each piece follows sideways by .6~1.2 (6% of the remaining gap per frame). The background shows the board’s css color through, so on a stage where the background color changes per section, the color bends through the glass
ease: none · follows the cursor 6% per frame

options.drift: Distance that flows per screen of scroll (stage units), default 1.2 — 0 means stay in place

note: three.cjs loads after ../pillar-gallery-gl/three-global.js as a plain script <script> ...loaded as such. It is a transmissive material, so best used once per panel — it is not drawn when off screen

from.where: All pages fixed stage behind (.l-stage) glass pieces — the original’s canvas
